elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence".

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "... and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate".

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000".

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "where TrueLink processes any data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Client, cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000" — the trigger reaches every category of Client data rather than selected named types.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "and workers' compensation insurance as required by law".

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "TrueLink shall provide certificates of insurance upon Client's request."

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: E&O at USD 2,000,000 exceeds the USD 1,000,000 fallback floor.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Cyber and privacy liability at USD 5,000,000 exceeds the USD 2,000,000 fallback floor.

reasons: The Agreement contains no insurance covenant anywhere (Sections 13–30 and the charges-only exhibits), so a concise insertion is the correct treatment for a 'missing' finding; all new words are necessary to build the clause.

All six preferred elements appear in operative language with the correct amounts, bases (per occurrence / aggregate) and party direction (TrueLink as insuring party, Client as beneficiary of certificates).

The cyber trigger is drafted broadly ('any data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Client'), satisfying the requirement that the Customer Data insurance trigger cover every category of Client data rather than selected named types.

Minimality holds: the drafter omitted the model language's 'at its own expense' and the one-year survival tail, added no procedures, notice mechanics, additional-insured or waiver-of-subrogation extras, and deleted nothing from the retained text (Section 30 force majeure is reproduced verbatim).
Intent is preserved: the insertion sits after the final section, creates no undefined term, no dangling cross-reference, and does not contradict any retained allocation, remedy or timing provision.

Drafting nit only (not a defect in the checklist): the inserted heading reads 'INSURANCE.' without a section number while every other provision is numbered — number it '31.' for consistency before sending.
